newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - SHARES UP, DOMESTIC INVESTORS RE-EMERGE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - SHARES UP, DOMESTIC INVESTORS RE-EMERGE.

text.p: Lithuanian shares continued their slow rise on Wednesday with Rokishkis Cheese, Birzai Milk and Vilniaus bank active, dealers said.
"The trade on the bourse shows a slow but stable rise," said Grazhina Bachiuliene, a dealer with Vilfima brokerage house.
"There was some hesitation among domestic investors after the price falls in February, but they are coming back to the market now," said Tomas Andrejauskas, a dealer at brokerage House Suprema.
"Investors are anticipating good results in most of the blue chip stocks," he told Reuters.
The bourse's group A index rose 12.87 points to 2,483.98 and turnover on the central market was 1.28 million litas.
Vilniaus bank's ordinary shares advanced 8.7 percent to 250 litas from 230 litas on turnover of 115,000 litas.
Hermis bank edged down to 195 litas from 200 litas on turnover 97,600 litas while Ukio bank stepped down to 19.25 litas from 20 litas in tiny turnover of 15,958 litas.
"Activity of dairy companies stocks was very high today," Bachiuliene said.

Birzai Milk diary advanced to 10.5 litas from 10 litas in turnover of 227,671 litas and official bourse list candidate Rokishkis Cheese saw its shares rise to 43 litas from 42 litas in turnover of 155,875 litas.
The two dairies made up the bulk of the bloc trade, which overall totalled 602,614 litas.
Turnover in Rokishkis Cheese totalled 430,000 litas at a price of 43 litas. Birzai Milk dairy saw its shares change hands in a deal worth 157,500 litas at a price of 10.5 litas.
Lithuanian Gas edged up to 2.20 litas from 2.19 litas on 198,297 litas turnover.
The trade with government T-bills amounted to 121,098 litas.
